title: OAuth2, OpenID Connect and Google Login
summary: Use managed Google OIDC login and keep local account permissions separate.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: OAuth2 in Spring Boot | How to Add Google Login in Spring Boot | Complete Tutorial

richText: OAuth2 grants access; OpenID Connect adds identity
OAuth2 lets a client request limited access to a resource. A scope names the requested access. OpenID Connect (OIDC) adds login identity using an ID token and the openid scope.
The client is your application. Google is the provider. The browser redirects the user to Google. Your server never needs the user’s Google password.
An access token is for an API. An ID token describes an authenticated user for a client. Do not treat any token from any provider as an access token for your own journal API.
For a server-rendered application, choose oauth2Login and a server session. For a separate API accepting access tokens, configure a resource server. They solve different parts of the flow.
Add spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client. Register an OAuth client with Google and register the exact callback URI. Spring’s default callback path is /login/oauth2/code/google.
Supply the client ID and secret through environment configuration or a secret manager. Keep the secret on the server. Do not place it in browser code or commit it to source control.
The google registration name selects Spring’s built-in provider defaults. Request openid, profile and email for OIDC login.

spring:
  security:
    oauth2:
      client:
        registration:
          google:
            client-id: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}
            client-secret: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}
            scope: openid,profile,email
Spring starts login at /oauth2/authorization/google. It keeps the authorization request, handles the callback, exchanges the code and validates the OIDC response.
The configuration below permits login routes and requires login for application routes. Keep CSRF protection because authenticated browser requests use a session cookie.
Map provider identity to local permissions
Identify an external account by the verified issuer and subject (sub). Email can change. Assign local roles through your application’s account policy. Google login does not automatically grant ADMIN.
The authorization request and response must belong to the same login attempt. The state parameter protects this association. Use Spring’s flow rather than building an unvalidated callback handler.

The tutorial repository manually exchanges a code, calls Google tokeninfo, finds or creates a user by email, and returns its own JWT. It also uses an OAuth Playground redirect. This is a learning demonstration.

Google documents tokeninfo as a debugging tool. Production verification must check signature, audience, issuer and expiry using a supported verifier. A successful tokeninfo response alone is not a complete local account-linking policy.
